# Breaking on check

`check_key` decides ACCEPTED or DENIED. Stop it while it runs.

## 1. Resolve and break

Read `check_key`'s address from `FrSj` (yours will differ), then:

```text
[0x00000000]> Frbj 0x5c95c467e209
{"ok":true,"result":{"address":"0x5c95c467e209","bp":1}}

[0x00000000]> Frbj
{"ok":true,"result":{"breakpoints":[{"bp":1,"address":"0x5c95c467e209"}]}}
```

Breakpoints use frida's `Interceptor.attach`: no plugin-side patching, no
slot cap, they fire on **every thread**, and Frida may rewrite the prologue.

## 2. Trigger

In the demo's terminal, feed a wrong key. The thread entering `check_key`
parks:

```text
[0x00000000]> Frmj
{"ok":true,"result":{"messages":[...,{"kind":"send","payload":{"type":"Fr.bp","bp":1,"address":"0x5c95c467e209","threadId":46117,"context":{}}}],"dropped":0}}
```

The demo is now frozen at the breakpoint, waiting for you.

![Breakpoint hit](img/native_journey/bp-check.png)

## 3. Inspect the stop

```text
[0x00000000]> FrBj 46117
{"ok":true,"result":{"threadId":46117,"bp":1,"address":"0x5c95c467e209"}}
```

Same as on Android: the stop identity only, no register values.

## 4. Write a register

```text
[0x00000000]> FrBj 46117 rip 0x414141414141
{"ok":true,"result":{"threadId":46117,"register":"rip","value":"0x414141414141"}}
```

The write mutates the parked thread's live context. (Setting rip to garbage
here is just a demo, an actual patch would point the flow somewhere useful.)
Type the register name.

## 5. Continue

```text
[0x00000000]> Frgj 46117
{"ok":true,"result":{"resumed":true,"threadId":46117}}
```

The demo resumes and prints its verdict. Clean up:

```text
[0x00000000]> Frb-j *
{"ok":true,"result":{"removed":1}}
```

## How the parking works

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
    participant T as target thread
    participant A as agent
    participant H as host
    T->>A: enters check_key (onEnter)
    A->>H: Fr.bp event (bp, address, threadId)
    A->>A: park: recv('Fr.cont.<tid>').wait()
    H->>H: FrBj stop identity or write live context
    H->>A: Fr.cont.<tid> request
    A->>T: resume the function
```

The agent parks the thread with a `recv` on a per-thread channel
(`Fr.cont.<tid>`), so continuing a specific thread is deterministic, and
the host keeps the thread's live Interceptor context for a register write.

> **Note:** the breakpoint's `context` is intentionally empty in the event:
> the full serialized CPU context can exceed the transport limit on arm64.
> The context for register work is kept inside the agent.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Try

Break on `check_key`, feed a wrong key, read the stop, write a register,
continue. Repeat with the real key.
:::
